Aria: Quick sync — alternate idea to RFC-2025. Instead of per-layer free-form hints, what about 'band profiles' that group layers by sensitivity (headwise/ffn) and map each band to a small bitwidth option set. This reduces kernel combinatorics. Thoughts?

Sam: Banding seems practical. How do we compute sensitivity bands? Offline metric like delta-perplexity-per-bit on a calibration suite? Or online clustering from telemetry?

Aria: Calibration suite initially. We can also have an adaptive rebanding job that runs nightly to shift layer membership if traffic patterns differ.

Diego: We must be careful with customer overrides. If they pin 'no banding changes' we should respect it. Also consider per-model vs per-endpoint bands.

Priya: Operationally, bands help versioning: manifest lists bands and allowed bitwidths. Runtime only needs kernels for band+bitwidth pairs, much smaller. Example manifest snippet: 

```
bands: [
  {name: "attn_sensitive", layers: [0,2,4], allowed: ["fp8","int8"]},
  {name: "ffn_lo", layers: [3,5..11], allowed: ["int4","int8","fp8"]}
]
```

Aria: Exactly. Also add shape predicate overrides: band "attn_sensitive" can say seq_len>1024 => only fp8.

Sam: What about mixed head behaviours inside attention? Some heads degrade more than others under int4. We might need headwise hints for extreme cases, but keep headwise as opt-in advanced knob.

Diego: Telemetry: store band-level quality signals rather than per-layer to save space. But we must retain ability to drill down when auditing.

quant-bot: Quick check: nightly rebanding job increased int4 usage by 12% without significant quality regressions on 100-sample checks. See /ops/reports/reband-2026-03. :robot_face:

Priya: Nice. Action items: Aria will add band profiles section to draft RFC. Sam to add rebanding job design. Diego to spec endpoint override flags. I'll add audit logging fields.

Aria: Thanks team. We'll merge into RFC-2025 follow-up doc.

Sam: +1

Diego: +1

Priya: +1
